title: PM chairs 54th PRAGATI Meeting
subtitle:
PM reviews infrastructure projects worth over ₹16,000 crore across 31 States and UTs
PM calls for faster redevelopment of major railway stations as multimodal transport hubs
PM emphasizes the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs
PM asks Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to improve welfare delivery
PM says focus should be on outcomes rather than on outlays to improve citizens’ lives
PM calls for linking Ekta malls with tourism and local businesses
body_text: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes. During the meeting, Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks covering 31 States/ UTs and costing more than 16 thousand crores. These projects, pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, were reviewed with a focus on timelines, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution. Prime Minister underlined that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He called for linking the malls with tourism and local businesses, noting that increased demand could create employment in rural production, packaging, storage and transportation. He stressed on review of progress regularly by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls. Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Prime Minister stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance. Prime Minister asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, he highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty. During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, PM called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks. Prime Minister asked  the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule. **** MJPS/SS/VJ
